findings.reason: an unordered pair on the same module is the collision the map exists to prevent, and §15's mechanism rests on the fence model §13 replaces.
findings.text: s15 appears in `plan-section-declarations` but in no `plan-section-depends-on` entry, although it declares `reckon/_worker_fence.py` and `reckon/nested_launch.py` as write paths — the same two modules unlanded `s13` rewrites, whose allow-list fence was reverted on 19 November — and it is not upstream of `s10`, so a batch dispatch runs two nodes over one module with no gate between them and no ordering for the section that changes how jobs are submitted

findings.reason: the followup body is the ordering an orchestrator dispatches from, so it must either be rewritten with §15 or resolved in favour of the new one.
findings.text: the document change added a second open followup (`f-awoj-s28`) carrying the same `/reckon-build` prompt while leaving `f-awojcosf-001` open with its dispatch order "§9 follows §4. §10 runs last", which names neither §13 nor §14 nor §15, while the map now makes §13, §14 and §15 upstream of §10 — a dispatcher reading the older followup runs the stale order and §15 appears in no order anywhere

findings.reason: the node would either implement the named mechanism and fail its own gate, or invent an unnamed one; the test's stand-in must sit where the product resolves scheduler binaries or the deliverable must narrow to resolved paths.
findings.text: the "likely mechanism" is to mount the shim read-only over "every real scheduler binary the shim lookup would forward to", a fixed set of resolved paths, while the done-when installs "a stand-in scheduler installed at an absolute path outside the worktree" — a path in no lookup set, so an implementation of the stated mechanism leaves the stand-in reachable unfenced and the green arm of the test fails; the alternative is an interception of arbitrary absolute paths, which the section neither names nor bounds, so the endpoint and its measure do not meet

findings.reason: a done declaration resting on an unrun control is the plan's own evidence contradicting itself; either the control is run or §14 reopens.
findings.text: `s14` is declared `done`, but the section's own close comment records "the base-revision control was a local test, not a betelgeuse job" while §14's negative control is "at the base revision the betelgeuse job refuses with §12's message", so the section is closed on a control it did not run and no later reader can tell whether the guard fires on that partition

findings.reason: a defect with an owner nowhere in the plan cannot be dispatched or closed, so §15/§14's carrier can be refused by a flight schema that never learns the key.
findings.text: the same close comment records "the flight schema does not yet declare the fence_program key" as an unresolved defect and `f-awoj-s28` (plan.html:149) only says to "place" that report in the plan: no section owns declaring the key, no done-when acquires it, and §14 ships a carried setting the flight composition is recorded as not declaring

findings.reason: the section id resolves and the numbering is display-only, so this is a presentation nit rather than a defect a node acts on.
